name: Warp

surfaces.label: Warp app (terminal + built-in Warp Agent, in-process). One process for every tab; the shells and the agent all live under it. Channels: Stable, Preview, Dev, Local, OSS.

Warp Agent CLI: the `warp` command (binary warp-tui-<channel>), standalone terminal agent, no app needed. The name `warp` is shared with MinIO's S3 benchmark tool (`brew install minio-warp` installs bin/warp); exclude_args lists its subcommands, which the Warp CLI never accepts (its only subcommand is dump-settings-schema).
Oz CLI: `oz agent run` (deprecated for `warp` after end of September 2026). Bundled wrapper Warp.app/Contents/Resources/bin/oz execs the app binary with argv[0] set to the wrapper path.
Cloud agents (Automation Platform, 'Oz'): run on Warp or self-hosted infrastructure; nothing local to match

working_signals.name: NSProcessInfo activity (UserInitiated) with reason "Agent Mode request in-progress", owned by the Warp app process or the warp-tui process
working_signals.meaning: Held for the lifetime of each streaming request to the agent backend, in both the app and the Warp Agent CLI, and dropped when the stream ends or is dropped. It is per request, not per turn, and app-wide (not per tab), so it can flicker off while a long local tool call runs between two requests. The same request path also fires for passive suggestion requests. Warp logs 'Preventing sleep with reason: Agent Mode request in-progress' and 'No longer preventing sleep with reason: ...' at info level to ~/Library/Logs/warp.log (app) as a second view of the same edge. Read from source only, never seen in pmset because Warp is not installed here.

Weak fallback, INFERRED and unmeasured. The app is a Rust GPU-rendered UI whose whole tree includes every shell and every command you run, so it false-positives on any busy terminal command. tool_children and child_process are deliberately absent because the app always has a terminal-server helper and the CLI always has its own shell child.

waiting_signals.meaning: Warp Agent CLI writes these to its own stdout when it runs inside a Warp app pane (env WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION and WARP_CLIENT_VERSION both set). Only the hosting terminal can read them, so an outside observer such as MinMacs cannot. permission_request means blocked on approval, question_asked means the agent asked a question, permission_replied means the human answered. Other events in the same stream: session_start, prompt_submit, tool_complete, stop, stop_failure.

The app shows this as the tab status icon (working, blocked, completed, errored) and the notification mailbox category Request. Not exposed over any local API (warpctrl has no agent actions) and not confirmed to be flushed to warp.sqlite.

hooks.config: none for Warp's own agent. Warp instead consumes lifecycle events from OTHER agents via per-agent plugins (Claude Code, OpenCode) and native config (Codex) that emit the OSC 777 warp://cli-agent protocol.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry export for local interactive use. The source has an OTLP/HTTP traces exporter (app/src/tracing/native.rs), but it is opt-in for cloud-agent runs only: needs WARP_CLOUD_AGENT_OTLP_ENDPOINT plus a valid dispatch token, exports spans tagged cloud_agent under service name warp-cloud-agent, traces only. Regular product telemetry goes to Warp's own backend, not OTLP.

notes: Nothing was observed live: every process, path and signal is from docs, the public source (warpdotdev/warp, master as of 2026-09-29), Homebrew metadata, or the shipped Stable CLI binary inspected with strings (never run). Warp is two things: a host terminal for other agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and 12 more, which keep their own rows) and a harness in its own right (Warp Agent, in-process in the app, and standalone in the `warp` CLI). Inside the Warp app there is one process for all tabs, so a per-tab or per-session status cannot come from the process table. For the CLI the process maps 1:1 to a conversation, but the session id is only on argv after --resume, and whether that token equals agent_conversations.conversation_id is not confirmed. The main app binary is named for the channel (stable, preview, dev, warp, warp-oss), not 'warp'; the Stable executable is Contents/MacOS/stable, taken from source and build scripts, not from a shipped app bundle (the DMG was not opened). The probe only reads `--resume <id>` as two argv elements, which matches the documented `warp --resume TOKEN` but not clap's `--resume=TOKEN` form. Known false-positive and false-negative limits of the process patterns: (1) the name `warp` is not unique (MinIO warp); the tui surface therefore excludes MinIO subcommands and Warp's own one-shot/worker arguments, but a bare `warp` with no arguments from another product would still match and cannot be told apart from an idle Warp Agent CLI by argv[0] alone. (2) On the Local channel the app binary is also named `warp`, so its helper processes match the tui names; the probe hides them only because it keeps the outermost process, so a detector without that rule must keep the worker exclusions. (3) The oz surface matches `oz agent ...` by substring, so short-lived `oz agent list` style commands also match; only `oz agent run` is documented as a long-running local agent. (4) Session DB: the primary path is the App Group container, the old Application Support path is legacy/fallback; the standalone TUI adds a tui/ subfolder and may fall back to Application Support because a bare binary may not get the group container. None of these was observed on disk.
